papers.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
papers.summary: Presents EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model that maps an EEG window plus question/answer specification to typed readouts (CHOICE, NOUL, SCORE) from one jointly trained checkpoint. On held-out splits of 35 public sources it reports 54.08% balanced accuracy on Stieger2021 motor imagery, 70.45% on Sleep-EDF-SC sleep staging, 72.11% per-window seizure detection on CHB-MIT (0.825 AUROC), and 1.700 MAE on ds005292 pain ratings, with calibration reducing NLL and cutting batch-1 latency 1.94-fold versus a matched generative comparator.

papers.title: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
papers.summary: Introduces EEGJev, a fast single-pass decision model for multi-task EEG question answering, together with EEGJev-Bench covering six question types across 19 public EEG sources. On 13 test sources it achieved 99.70% accuracy selecting the label for the requested attribute (49.20% under uniform choice) and 62.04% balanced accuracy for the specific answer, with 95th-percentile response times shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions.

papers.title: Monitoring Reduced Vigilance Using an Eyeglass-Type EEG System.
papers.summary: Developed and validated a reduced-vigilance monitoring algorithm for a custom eyeglass-type EEG device across a two-phase experiment with 21 participants, identifying a low-alpha/high-beta ratio as a fatigue-sensitive index and combining theta-plus-alpha drowsiness and fatigue indices via subject-specific thresholds and a logical OR rule. In pseudo-real-time evaluation of 16 participants the fusion model reached 70.31% mean accuracy, 10.40% false-positive rate, 49.67% recall, and 81.80% precision, with recall lower after excluding prolonged eye-closure segments.

papers.title: Revisiting the First Night Effect of Polysomnography Using Wearable EEG Headbands in Older Adults with Sleep Disturbances
papers.summary: Examined the first night effect during home-based polysomnography in 58 community-dwelling older adults with sleep disturbances using up to seven nights of wearable EEG headband monitoring including one simultaneous HPSG night. HPSG nights showed about 35 minutes more wake after sleep onset, 21 minutes less N3 sleep, and 15% lower sleep efficiency (ps < .001), while total sleep time and REM did not differ, suggesting single-night PSG may overstate sleep disruption and understate deep sleep.

papers.title: The EEG-Respiratory Gap: a deep learning biomarker associated with long-term mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
papers.summary: Developed a deep-learning model (AHIbrain) estimating apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel using 22,044 polysomnograms (internal test r=0.88; external r=0.50-0.62) and derived two EEG-Respiratory Gap metrics, Delta-AHIbrain and AHIbrain,event-free. Among participants free of cardiovascular disease, both metrics were associated with all-cause and non-CVD mortality after adjustment for AHI and clinical risk factors, and AHIbrain,event-free was also associated with CVD mortality in the highest-versus-lowest quartile comparison.

papers.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.summary: Introduces EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 s of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 s of prior EEG plus subsequent audiovisual stimulus, pretrained on 2,584 h of EEG from 78 participants. Nonlinear recurrent forecasting outperformed history-aware linear baselines (correlation 0.261 vs 0.233, 3.3-s horizon advantage) and transferred to 23 of 24 unseen individuals after calibration, with ongoing EEG history dominating while a video-dependent component enabled visual-representation evaluation.

papers.title: Before synchrony: the unresolved specificity of neural oscillations across brains.
papers.summary: A commentary arguing that EEG hyperscanning research should move beyond descriptive inter-brain synchrony reports by accounting for 1/f aperiodic activity and transient oscillatory bursts, and should formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and regions.

papers.title: SDAT: Synergistic domain-adaptation tuning for parameter-efficient EEG analysis.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
papers.summary: Proposes Synergistic Domain-Adaptation Tuning (SDAT), a parameter-efficient framework combining MSSF and coefficient attention tuning with a class-aware domain adaptation module for cross-subject EEG analysis. Updating under 10% of parameters, SDAT outperformed full fine-tuning and state-of-the-art PEFT baselines on LaBraM, EEG-DINO, and REVE-Base across abnormality detection, clinical-event classification, and emotion recognition.

papers.title: Sleep EEG distinguishes learned from novel auditory cues without predicting memory retention in a targeted memory reactivation study
papers.summary: In an 81-participant targeted memory reactivation study, learned auditory cues elicited stronger sleep delta responses than novel sounds, but cue-induced delta, theta, and sigma power did not predict retention, and TMR did not improve memory. Retention was instead predicted by pre-sleep memory strength and encoding vividness (vividness effect depending on encoding theta power), with encoding and sleep EEG power unrelated and showing distinct topographies.

papers.title: Mitigating Sleep Inertia and Maintaining Neurobehavioral Performance in Shift Workers via Multisensory (Music and Light) Intervention: A Preliminary Field Study.
papers.summary: Preliminary field crossover study of a wearable multisensory device (sleep-promoting music before sleep, uplifting music plus blue light on awakening) in 17 railway shift workers, which maintained PVT response speed, reduced end-of-shift lapses, and was associated with longer sleep duration vs control. A separate 10-adult EEG study showed increased slow-to-fast power ratio during sleep-onset stimulation and transiently lower theta early in wake-up stimulation.

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.summary: Describes a protocol integrating two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, EEG, and EMG in freely moving tethered mice using a stable chronic cranial-window/electrode implant, with the retrosplenial cortex as target. The preparation yields cellular-resolution calcium signals with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measures and supports stimulation-aligned response analysis.

papers.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control.
papers.summary: Benchmarked shallow CNN and LIF/adaptive-LIF spiking neural networks for four-class EEG motor imagery decoding on the BNCI 2014-001 dataset and integrated the spiking model into a decoding-to-robot-control pipeline. Spiking models were far more noise-robust than the CNN: under global Gaussian noise CNN accuracy dropped 58.56% versus 0.80% for adaptive LIF, and with one electrode removed CNN lost 36.00% versus 0.34%.

papers.title: Condition-associated EEG signatures in N-back tasks: temporal dynamics, classification, and generalization.
papers.summary: Examined condition-associated EEG signatures in 15 healthy adults performing N-back level (1/2/3-back) and stimulus-pacing manipulations with an 8-channel setup, analyzing bandpower, workload indices, N2/P3b ERPs, and classifier generalization. P3b amplitude decreased with higher load and faster pacing; N-SPEED three-class decoding generalized more consistently than N-LEVELS, but cross-paradigm transfer did not survive correction and decoding was constrained by small sample and deterministic block order.

papers.title: Large-Scale Neural Slowing Measured with Electroencephalography Indexes Secondary Thalamic Degeneration in Stroke.
papers.summary: Parameterized resting-state EEG spectral abnormalities in 25 stroke patients and linked them to thalamic atrophy (MRI) and corticothalamic circuit dysfunction (computational model), finding increased aperiodic exponent and offset, lower alpha frequency, and reduced beta power consistent with broad thalamic disinhibition. Most abnormalities were strongly associated with ipsilesional thalamic atrophy despite no direct thalamic damage, supporting large-scale neural slowing as a clinically feasible biomarker.

papers.title: CFCR-Net: cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: Proposes CFCR-Net, a cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning framework that couples wavelet packet sub-band decomposition with adaptive cross-frequency graph learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection. On SEED-VIG it achieved 0.8831 accuracy, 0.9102 F1-score, and 75.2% cross-subject accuracy, with visualization showing fatigue-related connectivity reorganizing toward low-frequency dominance.

papers.title: Neurofeedback enhances a neural signature of selective attention to speech in cocktail-party settings
papers.summary: In a ~49-min EEG neurofeedback training, participants viewing their TRF-derived N1 amplitude enhanced the N1 response to attended audiobooks specifically in feedback channels, an effect absent in a sham-feedback control group; right fronto-central N1 enhancement correlated with speech-comprehension gains.

papers.title: PFedHASNet: A Personalized Federated Hybrid Analog-Spike Network for Multi-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Proposes PFedHASNet, a personalized federated learning framework combining analog temporal features, LIF spike responses, and channel-wise log-variance statistics in a shared encoder with client-private residual adapters and classifiers for multi-subject motor imagery EEG decoding. Across four public MI-EEG datasets it achieved the highest mean client macro-F1 among 18 configurations, with ablation studies confirming contributions of hybrid representations and personalization.

papers.title: Emotion recognition oriented to hierarchical brain networks: A contrastive learning-driven novel dual-geometric space framework.
papers.summary: Develops HBNet, a dual-geometric (Euclidean and hyperbolic) hierarchical brain network framework with band base representation, cross-band interaction enhancement, and dual-geometric cross-band contrastive learning for EEG emotion recognition. Experiments on public EEG emotion datasets show HBNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Mapping EEG Microstates Across Physiological States: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: PRISMA 2020 systematic review (91 studies, June 2019–June 2025) synthesizing EEG microstate duration, frequency, coverage, topography, and transition probabilities in healthy adults, reporting longest durations for microstates D and C and best-evidenced transitions B→A, B→C, B→D, and C→D as a step toward normative reference values.

papers.title: Generalizable mapping of the Epileptogenic Zone from interictal Intracranial EEG using an implant topology-aware Transformer
papers.summary: Developed an implant topology-aware transformer that combines interictal intracranial EEG features with electrode coordinates to map the epileptogenic zone, trained on 476 patients from three public datasets and tested on 216 patients from five independent centers, achieving median AUPRC 0.71 and AUROC 0.92 in Engel I patients and outperforming spike-rate and seizure-onset-zone baselines.

papers.title: Adult EEG Reactivity in Rat Offspring After an Uncomplicated Birth Is Not Significantly Altered by Gestational Antibiotics.
papers.summary: Tested adult Wistar rat offspring after uncomplicated birth following gestational antibiotics, probiotics, combined treatment, or control, quantifying EEG burst-suppression reactivity to photic stimulation. No significant group differences in burst count reactivity or burst-suppression reactivity index were found, providing no evidence of a long-term effect after uncomplicated birth.

papers.title: Task exposure and stimulation duration modulate HD-tDCS effects on working memory in older adults.
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover study of 39 healthy older adults tested 2-mA HD-tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for 10 or 20 min on two-back working memory and EEG spectral power. Change in discrimination sensitivity showed a Stimulation × Duration × Exposure interaction, with 10-min real stimulation improving Δd' under less task exposure but reducing it under more exposure, and no significant effect for 20-min stimulation.

papers.title: Multi-scale feature fusion and neural architecture search for electroencephalography-based affective-state recognition in public benchmark datasets.
papers.summary: The study evaluated MFANet, a multi-scale feature fusion and neural architecture search framework for EEG-based affective-state recognition, on the DEAP and DREAMER public datasets. On DEAP it achieved mean accuracies above 97% for valence, arousal, and dominance, improving over a convolutional-recurrent baseline by 10.17 and 10.87 percentage points with multi-scale fusion and the searched recurrent module, respectively.

papers.title: Resting-State Alpha Power and Cross-Hemispheric Beta Connectivity Are Associated With Individual Differences in Voice Identity Perception.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.summary: In 61 native Mandarin speakers, resting-state EEG spectral power and interchannel coherence were related to voice identity perception measured with the Sisu Voice Matching Test. In eyes-open recordings, alpha-band power was positively associated with telling-together accuracy, while cross-hemispheric beta coherence between right frontal and left temporo-parietal regions correlated with overall and pseudo-word performance; the beta coherence associations remained robust after controlling for domain-general cognitive factors, whereas the alpha power effect was attenuated.

papers.title: Hybrid coati-gozde optimization-based EEG channel selection for automated alcoholism detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: Proposed a hybrid COA-GOZDE optimization algorithm for EEG channel selection using EEMD-derived IMF statistical features and kNN, Random Forest, and MLP classifiers, achieving 94.6% alcoholism detection accuracy with only 14 of 61 channels (79.34% channel reduction) and outperforming GWO, HHO, WOA, and COA.

papers.title: Tactile Feedback Device Effects on Sensory-Motor Integration in Post-Stroke Finger Impairment: A Single-Case Experimental Multiple-Baseline Study.
papers.summary: A single-case experimental multiple-baseline study evaluated a tactile sensory substitution device delivering real-time fingertip friction feedback in three participants with post-stroke finger impairment, using Tau-U effect sizes. Large to very large improvements were observed in Purdue Pegboard performance (Tau-U = 0.80) and finger numbness NRS (Tau-U = 0.79), with preliminary case-specific EEG gamma power changes and improved sense of agency.

papers.title: Footwear-Related Modulation of Scalp EEG Theta/Alpha Ratio During Walking in Children: An Exploratory Within-Subject Study.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
papers.summary: An exploratory within-subject study of 37 typically developing children aged 6-7 years compared mobile EEG theta/alpha ratio during 10-m walking under barefoot, barefoot-style footwear, and conventional structured footwear conditions. Conventional structured footwear produced significantly higher global Theta/Alpha ratios than both barefoot conditions, which did not differ from each other, with no differences in absolute theta, alpha, or beta power.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms by which spaced learning promotes understanding
papers.summary: Tested whether spaced learning improves understanding by changing rather than strengthening memory traces, using a word-meaning derivation task with massed (2 h) versus spaced (48 h) study and delayed EEG testing. Spacing increased between-session revisions (35% vs 25%) and delayed recognition and explanatory fluency, with less similar late-retrieval EEG patterns for remembered words after spaced learning, linked to the fluency advantage.

papers.title: Effects of Baseline Correction Strategy on Cervical Raman Spectral Analysis in a Late-Gestation Rat Model.
papers.summary: Evaluated how different baseline correction strategies affect cervical Raman spectral metrics and biological inference in a rat model at gestational days 15 and 20. Moderately polynomial fitting and asymmetric least squares produced coherent, biologically consistent results, while automated high-degree fitting over-suppressed spectra and could reverse the inferred gestational direction.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of a psychotherapy-predictive electroencephalographic signature in PTSD.
papers.summary: Using high-density resting-state EEG from military veterans with PTSD, the authors developed a machine-learning treatment-predictive signature that generalized across prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy; the signature was dominated by theta-frequency connectivity differences and identified a putative psychotherapy-resistant subgroup.

papers.title: Automated Classification of Clinical EEG Reports as Normal or Pathological Using Natural Language Processing: A Multi-Centre Study
papers.summary: Evaluated three NLP models (fine-tuned PolBERT, TF-IDF SVC, CatBoost) for classifying 6,829 Polish clinical EEG reports as normal or pathological across seven binary and three-class tasks, using expert ratings as reference labels. PolBERT led on six of seven tasks (binary accuracy 0.876–0.952) and all models exceeded individual experts on one task, but performance depended on expert disagreement and label aggregation method.

papers.title: Clinician belief revision after a background electroencephalography biomarker report in a nurse-led first seizure clinic: the PRISTINE study
papers.summary: Measured clinician belief revision after receiving a background EEG biomarker (BioEP) report in a nurse-led first seizure clinic, with 86 adults and the consultant nurse changing seizure-probability category in 40% of 81 non-contributory EEG cases. Revision direction and magnitude followed ordered BioEP report bands, and an exploratory pathway comparison suggested improved rule-in classification versus routine EEG alone.

papers.title: Group-Level Cohesion Ratings Across a Fixed-Order Individual-to-Multiplayer Gaming Paradigm: An Exploratory Study.
papers.journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
papers.summary: Exploratory fixed-order study comparing group-level cohesion ratings after individual versus multiplayer gaming in 60 healthy young adults across 10 groups. Group cohesion scores were higher after the second multiplayer condition (23.55 vs 18.13), but the difference is confounded with order and time, and OpenPose and ancillary EEG observations are descriptive and hypothesis-generating only.

papers.title: Ergonomic evaluation of an age-friendly foot dorsiflexion stretching device for adults aged 55 years or older.
papers.summary: Evaluated a foot dorsiflexion stretching prototype in 20 adults aged 55 years or older, measuring walking sEMG, frontal EEG, and perceptual responses across footplate inclinations and stretch durations. A 22° inclination with 60-s exposure emerged as a candidate setting only for this prototype and sequence, with no optimum, functional benefit, or safety threshold established.

papers.title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: Inspired by the stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, the authors report a silver-nanowire-reinforced mesohydrous metallic gel (MSC) with >10^6 S m-1 conductivity, sub-micron thickness and dual electronic/ionic conduction that enables imperceptible skin electrophysiology and neuromuscular stimulation.

papers.title: Combining Peripheral Inflammatory Biomarkers and aEEG Background Monitoring to Predict Neurological Outcome in Neonates Undergoing Cardiac Surgery for Congenital Heart Disease: A Real-World Pilot Experience.
papers.summary: Retrospectively examined perioperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and monocyte-to-albumin ratio in 64 neonates with congenital heart disease undergoing cardiac surgery, relating them to aEEG background and short-term neurological outcome. NLR was consistently associated with worsening aEEG background and higher T2 NLR with unfavorable outcome, with combined NLR+aEEG yielding a non-significantly higher AUC of 0.844.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.summary: Across 33 pediatric epilepsy patients, three HPO profiles differing in EEG terms were compared for phenotype-driven variant prioritization; more specific EEG-related HPO terms were associated with lower phenotype and Exomiser scores and changed the top-ranked gene in 24-55% of patients, while the full profile produced the shortest candidate lists.

papers.title: Hypothesis-Driven Thalamic Stereo-EEG Informs Surgical Therapy for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Outcomes in 117 Consecutive Patients
papers.summary: Reviewed 117 consecutive patients undergoing hypothesis-driven thalamic SEEG (ANT, CM, PUL) to assess safety, targeting accuracy, and how thalamic ictal timing informs laterality and neuromodulation targeting. Thalamic SEEG showed low symptomatic hemorrhage rates, revised pre-SEEG neuromodulation targets in 34.6% of planned RNS cases, and early thalamic ictal signals were associated with better seizure outcomes after thalamic/thalamocortical RNS.

papers.title: Flavor quality changes in fermented shrimp paste under different sterilization strategies: An integrated flavoromics and neural perception approach.
papers.summary: Integrated flavoromics with EEG-based neural perception to compare pasteurization, retort sterilization, ultrasound-assisted infrared sterilization, and ultra-high-pressure instantaneous sterilization effects on fermented shrimp paste flavor. Ultra-high-pressure instantaneous sterilization preserved glutamate-IMP synergy and umami intensity above traditional fermentation, with dimethyl trisulfide and trimethylpyrazine as key differential aroma markers and UPI/UIR eliciting pleasantness-like EEG theta/alpha responses.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary rescue and evidence-based nursing intervention for severe postoperative hypoxemia in a former preterm infant: a case report.
papers.summary: Case report describing multidisciplinary rescue and evidence-based nursing of a former 32-week preterm infant who developed severe postoperative hypoxemia (SpO₂ minimum 29%) with apnea after inguinal hernia surgery. A closed-loop warning-intervention-evaluation model, corticosteroids, nebulization, and early HHFNC were temporally associated with avoidance of reintubation, with discharge on day 8 and no events at 1-week follow-up.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
